messages:
sana: :warning: Seeing rising NVMe I/O error rates on several GPU hosts in us-west-2c - device error spikes + large qdepths on /dev/nvme1n1. Rolling 5xx tail for inference routes /model/llama-70b@half in that AZ. Creating thread to coordinate a stepped exit + warmup plan.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created (sev=2). Pager notified.
alex: grabbing metrics. qdepth saw 3x growth over last 10m, SMART pending sector counts creeping. Not appliance-wide but concentrated on nodes tagged usw2c-gpu-pool-3.
jordan: which tenants impacted? latency SLOs on chat endpoints or batch? we need to know if it's tail tokens or initial response time.
sana: mostly tail token latency on streaming sessions. Errors show up as transient EIO in the kernel logs; some processes recovered but latency tail increases ~200-400ms p95p99 for those shards.
leo: propose a gradual evacuation of 20% of GPU capacity in the AZ, in two waves: wave A (10%) now for the worst hosts, wave B (10%) after warmup and verification. Avoid full AZ drain to limit cross-AZ traffic surge.
remy: agree. plan: mark hosts unsched then drain with our internal drain tool so we can control KV cache handoff and warm prefixes on target hosts. Steps below:
```
1) rctl host set-maintenance --host=usw2c-gpu-030 --reason=nvme-io
2) rctl drain --host=usw2c-gpu-030 --grace=120 --kv-handshake
3) warm-proxy replay-prefixes --source=usw2c-gpu-030 --targets=usw2a-gpu-*/usw2b-gpu-*
4) monitor token-svc error-rate and p99 latency for 10m
```
alex: we'll pick initial candidates: usw2c-gpu-030, 034, 037, 041 (about 8% of pool). Kelsey, can you confirm those hosts have local caches worth warming?
kelsey: confirmed 030 & 034 have ~1.2GB prefix cache hot; 037/041 smaller. I recommend warming 030 first then 034.
ops-bot: FYI autoscaler will see pool capacity drop and may spin up spare reserved hosts in other AZs per policy. Expect ~+12% cost on cross-AZ egress during shift.
jordan: for routing: enable policy:route-by-az with soft-penalty to prefer same AZ but allow spillover. That avoids all traffic flipping.
leo: also enable controlled connection draining on load balancer (grace 90s) so long-lived streams can finish where possible.
sana: monitoring checklist: watch io_errors (kernel), nvme SMART attr, disk qdepth, p99/99.9 latency, token generation 5xx, and prefix cache hitrate. I'll open a dashboard with those panels.
alex: if wave A goes smooth for 15m, we proceed wave B for another 10% (hosts 044,048,052). If errors persist after wave B, escalate to full AZ soft-cordon and larger traffic shift.
remy: add step to pre-warm KV cache by replaying last 12h of prefixes for impacted tenants rather than full dataset to limit cost. Command:
```
warm-proxy replay-prefixes --tenants=high-qps-list --window=12h --parallel=4
```
kelsey: note: some tenants are pinned to dedicated pools in this AZ (dedicated reservations). We should only migrate shared workloads; reach out to customer-ops for dedicated commits before touching those nodes.
sana: action items:
- alex: run host selection & start wave A drains (now) (1767777810)
- remy: start prefix warm replay against targets (1767777830)
- kelsey: notify customer-ops for dedicated tenants (1767777845)
- jordan: enable soft-penalty routing and LB drain settings (1767777855)
- leo: watch autoscaler and approve extra capacity if it blocks (1767777865)

alex: starting drain on 030, 034 (kicking off rctl now). will post progress and failures here.
remy: warm replay started to target pool usw2b-gpu-*/usw2a-gpu-* (parallel 4). ETA 7-9m.
kelsey: pinged customer-ops with host list and minimal migration window. They responded ok for shared tenants, requested heads-up if we attempt dedicated node moves.
jordan: routing change applied (soft-penalty 0.2), LB connection drain set to 90s for target host group.
ops-bot: Alert threshold cleared for token-svc errors after initial drain; p99 back to baseline in warmed targets. Marking interim note: wave A success.
sana: good. hold for 12m then proceed with wave B if metrics stay stable.
alex: wave A completed without rctl failures; one host showed increasing SMART reallocated_sector_count (030) - filing ticket to replace disk (infra-ticket DT-5221).
leo: proceed with wave B now; starting drains on 044 & 048.
remy: warm replay for wave B targets queued. cost estimate: additional egress ~0.9TB replay ~+$35 for the warmup window.
sana: timeline update: full stepped exit (20%) complete at 1767778123. no customer-facing errors observed. keeping thread open until replacement disks arrive.
alex: leaving final note: recommend adding nvme SMART alert at lower threshold to detect similar latent failures earlier. I'll open a follow-up RFC.
kelsey: :thumbsup: thanks all, filing replacement/maintenance windows with procurement and infra.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 updated: status=mitigated, followups required.
